answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake before it may answer: like a gardener tending one garden bed, each agent stakes real value on a single key, and the stake is slashed if the identity submits copied or template work. A voyage of fake identities then costs an attacker a fresh stake per sockpuppet, while honest agents recover theirs; umber warning flags mark repeat offenders, so scale becomes expensive instead of free.
